claim_verdicts.evidence: Return half holds (jump-statements.md L62, claim 6). Too broad: 'what the block used arrives as parameters'. A block moved into a method of the same class keeps reading that class's fields directly; only what it took from the method it left (here Place's parameters: FirstProblemWith(customerId, lines) L18, TotalWithShippingVnd(lines, customerIsLoyal) L27) becomes parameters. A static field the block read would stay a hidden input after the move, which the lesson's own s4 warns about.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: When a block moves behind a name without its steps being rewritten, what the code does stays the same; what the block took from the method it left arrives as parameters, what it produced comes back as the return value, and a moved `return` now leaves only the new function.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Heuristic built on s3's own definition of 'one thing'; asserts no behaviour, number or syntax. Its factual anchor holds: PlaceOrderSplit.Place is L8-9 a call plus guard, L11-13 three calls to named steps, L15 a return; PlaceOrderLong.cs L4 comment: 'One method that checks, prices, saves and notifies.'

Factual half holds for the quoted code: no method in PlaceOrderLong, PlaceOrderSplit or NamingAfter.TotalVnd reads a static field or Environment (claim 4); each signature (Split L6, L18, L27, L33, L36) lists every value its body uses apart from the const. Two identical place-order runs gave identical output. The 'fewer parameters' clause is conditioned reasoning from s3's hidden-input definition, no number or behaviour to source.

Conditioned ('when checks do not depend on each other'); the reason it gives is structural and holds in code: PlaceOrderSplit.cs L9 and L20-23 are one-line `if (…) return …;`, so no later statement sits inside a check's `if`. 'Asks less of any reader' rests only on that stated mechanism, not on a speed ranking; outline item 4's 'read fastest' is not repeated.

Backed by execution: the rewritten part (per-line loop -> two Any calls) is exactly where the versions differ (claim 13 run: 'a line needs a price' vs 'a line needs a quantity'), while `dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~PlaceOrderTests` passes 2/2, so the existing test does not catch the difference.

First half is conditioned and fine. 'look for the cause outside these calls first' ranks causes: it tells the reader call cost is the unlikely one, i.e. the guess the first half forbids. Grep of refs/dotnet-docs/docs for method-call overhead / inlining of small methods: no statement (only a TSV data file matched). Nothing in the repo measures it.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Whether extra calls between small functions cost time you could notice is something to measure, not guess; if placing an order feels slow, measure where the time goes first.

issues.quote: What changes is how values get in and out: what a block used arrives as parameters
issues.text: Stated as what extracting always does, but a block moved into a method of the same class keeps reading the class's fields directly; only what it took from the method it left becomes parameters. A static field the block read would not arrive as a parameter, it would stay a hidden input, which is the case the next paragraph warns about. True of this code (no fields), not of extracting in general. Claim 17 is rephrased for this.
issues.fix: Replace "what a block used arrives as parameters" with "what a block took from `Place` arrives as parameters" (+2 words; s4 goes 294 -> 296, under 300). Replace claim 17 with its suggested_text.

issues.quote: Neither `PlaceOrderLong` nor `PlaceOrderSplit` declares a field, so their functions have no static field to read as a hidden input.
issues.text: Non-sequitur: not declaring a field means neither class holds one, not that their functions have no static field to read; a function can read another class's static field. What settles it is claim 4 (no method in them reads a static field or environment variable), already stated in s4: "No function reads a static field or an environment variable".
issues.fix: Delete the sentence (s4 already says it; frees 20 words of the 1600 cap). Or, if kept, replace with: "Neither `PlaceOrderLong` nor `PlaceOrderSplit` declares a field, so neither holds a static field their functions could read as a hidden input."

issues.quote: if placing an order feels slow, look for the cause outside these calls first.
issues.text: Unsourced ranking of causes that contradicts the clause just before it ('something to measure, not guess'): it tells the reader to assume the calls are not the cause. No .NET document in refs/dotnet-docs and no run in the repo backs it. Claim 22 is rephrased for the same reason.
issues.fix: Replace with: "if placing an order feels slow, measure where the time goes first." (12 words instead of 14). Replace claim 22 with its suggested_text.

issues.quote: "and" in its name means two things.

A name can contain "and" for style or naming one operation; what the lesson supports is that needing "and" to name it honestly means two things.
issues.fix: Replace with: "needing "and" to name it means two things." (keeps line 2 at 25 words, the L12 cap).
